title: Erdős Problem #417: Counting Totient Values
description: Does the limit V(x)/V'(x) exist, where V'(x) counts distinct totients from inputs at most x and V(x) counts all totient values at most x?

meta.author: Erdős (1979, 1998)
originalContributions: Defined V'(x) and V(x) counting functions for totient values
Stated three OPEN questions about V(x)/V'(x) ratio
Proved 1 and p-1 (prime p) are totient values
Proved powers of 2 are totient values via φ(2^(k+1)) = 2^k
Characterized odd numbers > 1 as non-totient values
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: erdos_417_conjecture (Erdős conjecture that V(x)/V'(x) → ∞, OPEN). Previously had 3 axioms; erdos_417_limit_exists removed (inconsistent with conjecture), erdos_417_ratio_gt_one proved from conjecture.

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős first posed this problem in [Er79e], asking about two natural counting functions for Euler's totient values. Given the set of all totient values, one can count how many appear among outputs of small inputs ($V'(x)$) versus how many totient values exist up to $x$ regardless of input size ($V(x)$). The question is whether these two counts grow at comparable rates.

The problem was revisited in Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] in their influential monograph on combinatorial number theory. In [Er98], Erdős went further and conjectured that $V(x)/V'(x)$ may actually tend to infinity, suggesting that the vast majority of totient values at most $x$ come from inputs much larger than $x$. This would be a striking statement about the structure of the totient function's range.

The problem connects to deep results on totient value density. Pillai (1929) first showed $V(x) = o(x)$. Erdős (1935) proved $V(x) \sim cx/\log x$. Ford (1998) determined the precise asymptotics: $V(x) = \frac{x}{\log x} \exp(C_1(\log_3 x)^2 + C_2 \log_3 x + C_3)$. However, the relationship between $V(x)$ and $V'(x)$ remains open, as it requires understanding the **smallest preimage function** $m^*(n) = \min\{m : \varphi(m) = n\}$. Related questions appear in Problem #416, which concerns the structure of the totient range more directly.
overview.problemStatement: Let $V'(x) = |\{\varphi(m) : 1 \le m \le x\}|$ count the distinct totient values achievable from inputs at most $x$, and let $V(x) = |\{n \le x : n = \varphi(m) \text{ for some } m\}|$ count all totient values at most $x$. Does $\lim_{x \to \infty} V(x)/V'(x)$ exist? Is it $> 1$? Erdős conjectured it may be $\infty$.
overview.text: Does the limit V(x)/V'(x) exist, where V'(x) counts distinct totients from inputs at most x and V(x) counts all totient values at most x?
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines both counting functions $V'(x)$ and $V(x)$ using `Finset` operations on the range of Mathlib's `Nat.totient`. The `IsTotientValue` predicate captures membership in the totient range. We prove the trivial inequality $V'(x) \le V(x)$, characterize which numbers are totient values (odd numbers $> 1$ are excluded, all powers of 2 and prime predecessors are included), and state the three open questions using `Filter.Tendsto` for limits and `Filter.atTop` for asymptotic behavior.
keyInsights: **Trivial inequality $V'(x) \le V(x)$**: Every totient from $m \le x$ is also a totient value $\le x$, but $V(x)$ may include totients from large $m > x$ (e.g., $\varphi(2^{10}) = 512$ contributes to $V(600)$ but not $V'(600)$)

**Parity obstruction**: Odd numbers $> 1$ are never totient values because $\varphi(m)$ is even for $m > 2$, so only even numbers and 1 can be totients---this eliminates roughly half of all integers from the range

**Smallest preimage problem**: The conjecture $V(x)/V'(x) \to \infty$ is equivalent to asking whether $m^*(n) = \min\{m : \varphi(m) = n\}$ is typically much larger than $n$, so that most totient values $n \le x$ have $m^*(n) > x$

**Ford's precise asymptotics**: $V(x) = \frac{x}{\log x} \exp(C_1(\log_3 x)^2 + C_2 \log_3 x + C_3)$ gives the exact order of the totient value counting function, but the analogous formula for $V'(x)$ is unknown

**Connection to Carmichael's conjecture**: The open conjecture that every totient value has multiplicity $\ge 2$ (i.e., $|\varphi^{-1}(n)| \ne 1$ for all $n$) is related to the structure of preimages that drives the $V/V'$ ratio

sections.title: Module Header and Overview
sections.summary: File header for Erdős #417 (OPEN): with $V'(x)=|\{\varphi(m):m\le x\}|$ (distinct totient values from small inputs) and $V(x)=|\{n\le x: n\in\operatorname{range}\varphi\}|$ (totient values up to $x$), does $V(x)/V'(x)$ have a limit, and is it $>1$ (Erdős conjectured $\infty$)? Imports Mathlib, opens `Nat`/`Set`/`Filter`/`Finset`, enters the `Erdos417` namespace.
sections.mathContext: $V'(x)\le V(x)$; the ratio measures density of totient values vs. their appearances. Erdős conjectured $V(x)/V'(x)\to\infty$.

sections.title: Part I: Basic Definitions
sections.summary: Defines the two counting functions `V'` and `V`, and the predicate `IsTotientValue n` ($n$ is in the range of Euler's totient).

sections.title: Part II: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Structural facts: `V'_le_V`, monotonicity (`V'_mono`, `V_mono`), positivity (`V'_pos`, `V_pos`), small totient values (`one_/two_/four_is_totient_value`), `zero_not_totient_value`, and `odd_gt_one_not_totient` ($\varphi(m)$ is even for $m>2$).
sections.mathContext: $V'\le V$, both monotone and positive; no odd $n>1$ is a totient value.

sections.title: Part III: The Main Questions
sections.summary: Formalizes the open problem: `erdos417LimitExists`, `erdos417RatioGtOne`, and `erdos417ConjectureInfinite`. The axiom `erdos_417_conjecture` asserts the (open) infinite-limit conjecture, from which `erdos_417_ratio_gt_one` follows.
sections.mathContext: Conjecture (axiomatized): $V(x)/V'(x)\to\infty$; in particular the ratio exceeds 1.

sections.title: Part IV: Intuition for the Conjecture
sections.summary: Commentary on why the ratio should grow: $V(x)$ counts all totient values $\le x$ regardless of input size, while $V'(x)$ only counts those reachable from inputs $\le x$.
sections.mathContext: Large totient values $\le x$ may require inputs $\gg x$, inflating $V$ relative to $V'$.

sections.title: Part V: Connection to Problem #416
sections.summary: Relates this problem to the sibling Erdős Problem #416 on the distribution of totient values.
sections.mathContext: Problem #416 studies the multiplicity/distribution of totient values, closely tied to counting them here.

sections.title: Part VI: Totient Value Structure
sections.summary: Concrete structure of totient values: `pow_two_totient_value` ($2^k=\varphi(2^{k+1})$), `prime_pred_totient_value` ($p-1=\varphi(p)$), `totient_zero_one_or_even`, `prime_sub_one_even` ($p-1$ even for $p\ge3$), and `V_element_structure`.
sections.mathContext: Totient values include all $2^k$ and all $p-1$; every totient value is $0$, $1$, or even.

sections.title: Part VII: Asymptotic Estimates
sections.summary: Commentary on the known asymptotics of $V(x)$ (the Erdős–Ford–Tenenbaum theory of the multiplicative structure of totient values) and what is needed to attack the ratio.

sections.title: Part VIII: Why This Is Hard
sections.summary: Discussion of the difficulty: controlling $V(x)/V'(x)$ requires fine understanding of how totient values are distributed relative to their preimages.
sections.mathContext: The ratio couples two different counts of totient values, each governed by delicate sieve/anatomy-of-integers estimates.

sections.title: Part IX: Summary
sections.summary: Recaps the status (OPEN) via `erdos_417_summary` and `erdos_417_open_questions`: the basic properties and totient-value structure are proved, while the limit existence and its value remain conjectural. Closes the namespace.
sections.mathContext: Status OPEN: $V(x)/V'(x)$ limit existence and value (conjectured $\infty$) remain unproven.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #417 investigates the ratio $V(x)/V'(x)$ of two counting functions for totient values. $V'(x)$ counts distinct totients achievable from inputs at most $x$, while $V(x)$ counts all totient values at most $x$. The trivial bound $V'(x) \le V(x)$ holds, but whether the ratio converges, exceeds 1, or tends to infinity as Erdős conjectured in 1998 remains completely open.
conclusion.implications: Understanding this ratio would reveal how the totient function's range is generated: whether small inputs efficiently cover most totient values or whether most values arise from unexpectedly large preimages. A resolution would connect Ford's precise asymptotics for $V(x)$ with the distribution of the smallest preimage function $m^*(n)$, bridging multiplicative number theory with questions about preimage structure of arithmetic functions.
openQuestions: What are the precise asymptotics of $V'(x)$? Is $V'(x) = o(V(x))$?
How does the smallest preimage function $m^*(n) = \min\{m : \varphi(m) = n\}$ distribute relative to $n$?
